newsitem.title: UK: No verdict on Hamilton in UK parl't sleaze report.
newsitem.headline: No verdict on Hamilton in UK parl't sleaze report.

text.p: An interim report by a parliamentary committee investigating allegations of sleaze by members of parliament on Thursday cleared 15 legislators, but deferred a verdict on former minister Neil Hamilton and several other Conservatives.

The Standards and Privileges Committee report looked set to fuel the flames of a pre-election row in which opponents have accused Prime Minister John Major of blocking publication of a fuller report by parliamentary commissioner Sir Gordon Downey.

The report said Downey had been unable to complete his report due to "the complexity of the web of accusations that have been made against certain members and the volume of evidence produced". The investigation concerned 25 MPs.
It said that in the case of 15 cleared, the position was straightforward and they had not broken any parliamentary rules on declaring their income from outside parliament.

The 15 include minority Liberal Democrat deputy leader Alan Beith, Doug Hoyle, the chairman of the parliamentary Labour party, defence secretary Michael Portillo, former cabinet minister David Mellor and Labour's health spokesman Chris Smith.

But the report said the investigation into allegations that MPs including Neil Hamilton, whom it did not name, were paid by Mohammed Al-Fayed, the owner of London's Harrods store, to ask questions in parliament on his behalf would not be finished in time for publication before the May 1 election.
